guidance_status: Provisional hand-authored routing policy; not benchmark-calibrated. Supported effort subset, not exhaustive.

effort_guidance.low: Short, explicit, routine work with little reasoning.
effort_guidance.medium: Several connected implementation steps with limited uncertainty.
effort_guidance.high: Complex diagnosis or interacting decisions requiring deeper reasoning.
effort_guidance.xhigh: Very difficult, long-running reasoning with multiple unresolved hypotheses.
effort_guidance.max: Exceptional capability-sensitive work; use only when lower effort is plausibly inadequate, not merely because the task is risky.

models.selection_guidance: Economical candidate for routine, well-specified, easily verified work.

Most efficient current OpenAI candidate for focused, well-specified, easily verified work; lowest price in the OpenAI lineup. Routing boundary (uncalibrated hypothesis): prefer for mechanical edits and focused work with known steps and direct checks. Unresolved cross-system diagnosis or novel algorithm research belongs to a stronger candidate.
Balanced candidate for scoped implementation and moderate debugging.
Flagship candidate for complex professional coding and interacting components.
Balanced current OpenAI candidate for complex coding and agentic workflows; priced below GPT-5.6 Sol.

Balanced OpenAI candidate for complex coding, computer use, and professional work; near-Astra capability at lower cost according to official guidance. Prefer over GPT-6 Sol for this role; compare with Astra on representative tasks. Routing positioning is provisional, not benchmark-calibrated. Routing boundary (uncalibrated hypothesis): prefer for scoped features and complex software engineering using established algorithms and implementation patterns, including ordinary multi-component debugging. Novel algorithm invention, competing unresolved research hypotheses or proof obligations beyond known patterns belong to Astra.

Most capable OpenAI candidate for difficult reasoning and hard end-to-end work. Routing boundary (uncalibrated hypothesis): prefer when the central work is novel algorithm invention, unresolved research hypotheses, proof/counterexample exploration, or exceptionally difficult reasoning beyond established implementation patterns. Routine edits and scoped features belong to Luna or Sol under balanced/cost policies.
Fast balanced candidate for scoped coding and moderate debugging.

Fast balanced candidate for scoped coding and moderate debugging; replaces Claude Sonnet 5 at the same price. Effort levels are recalibrated from Sonnet 5: medium suits well-specified agentic coding, high harder or longer work. Routing boundary (uncalibrated hypothesis): prefer for scoped features and debugging with known patterns and bounded tests. Unresolved causes across services and long-running architecture work belong to Opus; novel algorithm research belongs to Fable.
Candidate for complex agentic coding and enterprise work.

Current default Claude candidate for long-running agentic coding and knowledge work; priced below Claude Opus 5. Default effort is medium, so raise effort for demanding work. Routing boundary (uncalibrated hypothesis): prefer for complex cross-service diagnosis, concurrency, migrations and long-running implementation using established techniques. Scoped features belong to Sonnet; novel algorithm invention and unresolved proof-oriented research belong to Fable.

Candidate for demanding reasoning and long-horizon work beyond ordinary complex implementation. Routing boundary (uncalibrated hypothesis): prefer for novel algorithms, unresolved research hypotheses and proof/counterexample exploration beyond established implementation patterns. Ordinary scoped features belong to Sonnet and complex engineering with known techniques belongs to Opus.
Current flagship Grok coding candidate; tune effort to task difficulty. Only Grok model in the initial catalog, per current official general coding guidance.
Current flagship Grok coding candidate, recommended by xAI for code and all general use; tune effort to task difficulty (default high).
